ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
It is desired to find a three-tap causal filter which gives zero signal as an output to an input of the form 

\( x[n] = c_1 \exp \left(- \frac{j \pi n}{2}\right) + c_2 \exp \left(\frac{j \pi n}{2}\right) \) 

where \( c_1 \) and \( c_2 \) are arbitrary real numbers. The desired three-tap filter is given by 

\( h[0] = 1, \, h[1] = a, \, h[2] = b \) 

and 

\( h[n] = 0 \) for \( n < 0 \) or \( n > 2 \).

What are the values of the filter taps \( a \) and \( b \) if the output is \( y[n] = 0 \) for all \( n \), when \( x[n] \) is as given above?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: From the text, the input is a linear combination of two complex exponentials: e^{-jπn/2} and e^{jπn/2}. The three-tap FIR filter has h[0]=1, h[1]=a, and h[2]=b, so its frequency response is H(e^{jω})=1+a e^{-jω}+b e^{-j2ω}. Since c1 and c2 are arbitrary, each frequency component must be nulled individually. Thus H(e^{jπ/2})=0 and H(e^{-jπ/2})=0. For ω=π/2, H(e^{jπ/2})=1+a(-j)+b(-1)=1-ja-b=0. For ω=-π/2, H(e^{-jπ/2})=1+a(j)+b(-1)=1+ja-b=0. Subtracting the two equations gives -2ja=0, so a=0. Substituting back gives 1-b=0, hence b=1.
